transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm explaining this the right way, I've never really done this before. But, well, my boss actually suggested I come in. 

It's really not that bad, I promise, just... you know how it gets when things are busy? I've just been having a little trouble lately with, um, forgetting some scheduled callbacks and work orders. Just things slipping my mind. And I guess I missed some basic follow-ups I told people I'd do, so... it kind of piled up on me a bit recently. Work sent me here just to get it sorted out, because I have a shot at moving up to a better position and they don't want me to lose that chance over a few silly mistakes. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you're trying to focus on work tasks, do you find it hard to concentrate or keep your attention on one thing, or is it more that you can focus okay but just forget things afterward?

Well, um... I guess it might be a little bit of the first one? I mean, I really try my absolute best to focus, I do. But sometimes... well, like, I'll open up a digital work order, and I start reading the notes, thinking I've totally got it. But then halfway through reading, my mind just sort of... slips off. 

Like, I'll hear a noise somewhere in the building, or I'll start thinking about the next repair job I need to get to, and suddenly I realize I'm staring at the screen and I don't even know what I just looked at. 

I always go back and re-read it, of course! I'd never just ignore it, I always make sure the work gets done. It's just a silly little habit I have of getting a bit sidetracked while I'm looking at things. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples.
Do you experience these kinds of attention difficulties in other areas of your life outside of work—like when you're at home, with family or friends, or doing personal activities?

Oh, um... at home? I... I don't really think so. I mean, I haven't really noticed anything like that. 

When I'm home, I just try to relax or get my chores done, and I really try my best to be a good listener when I'm with my family. Maybe every now and then I'll misplace my keys or, you know, kind of space out for a second if I'm watching TV, but I figure that's just normal from being tired after a long shift on my feet, right? Everyone does that a little bit. 

So, no, I don't think it's a real problem outside of work. I try really hard to keep everything running smoothly at the house. Is that... is it okay if it's mostly just happening at my job? I hope I'm answering that the way you need me to.

When did you first start noticing these attention difficulties at work? Was it something that's been going on since you were younger, or is this something more recent that started within the last few months or year?

Oh... um... well. I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it's not exactly a new thing. I... I kind of remember being a bit like this way back in grade school, honestly. Long before I had any of this job pressure to worry about. 

I mean, my teachers always told my parents I was a bright girl! I really tried to be a good student, I did. It's just... I had a silly habit of misplacing my papers, or maybe missing parts of the directions when they were talking to the class. They'd have to remind me to finish my classwork sometimes because I'd just sort of drift off. 

I always meant well, I promise, I just needed a little extra nudge back then. Is it... is it bad that it's been going on since I was little? I hope that doesn't make things too complicated for you to help me.

When you were in grade school and your teachers mentioned you drifting off or needing reminders, do you remember if you were also feeling worried or anxious back then, or was it more just that your mind would wander regardless of how you were feeling emotionally?

Oh, um... no, I don't really think I was worried about anything back then. I was actually a very happy little girl! I didn't have any reason to be anxious or upset, you know? My parents were great and I really liked my teachers. 

It was more just... well, my mind would just sort of go on its own little adventures, regardless of how I was feeling. Even on a perfectly good day when everything was fine, I'd just kind of find myself staring out the window or thinking about a game I wanted to play later. It was never because I was nervous or anything like that. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just wouldn't want you to think I had a troubled childhood or anything, because I really didn't! I was just a bit of a daydreamer, if that's an okay answer for you.

When you're sitting at your desk working or in meetings, do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, like moving around in your chair, tapping your fingers, or feeling restless? Or do you tend to stay pretty still?

Oh, um... well, since I do maintenance work, I'm actually on my feet for most of my shift, so I don't really have a desk. But when we do have to sit down for, like, our morning safety meetings or when I'm filling out my work orders... no, I don't really fidget or anything like that. 

I try to be very polite and just sit quietly. I'm not really restless in my chair or tapping my feet or anything. I mean, my mind might be wandering off a little bit, like I mentioned before, but my body stays pretty still. I really wouldn't want to be disruptive or rude to anyone else in the room, you know? 

So, yeah, I tend to stay pretty still. I hope that's a good thing? I just try my best to be respectful when other people are talking.

Do you find yourself doing things without thinking them through first—like interrupting people, making quick decisions you later regret, or acting on impulse? Or do you tend to think things through before you act?

Oh, um, no, I really don't think I do that. I always try to be very careful about not interrupting people. I'd hate to make anyone feel like I wasn't listening to them or that what they had to say wasn't important, you know? 

I think I'm actually pretty cautious. I like to think things through before I do them, especially at work. I wouldn't want to make a quick decision and mess up a repair or cause a problem for the rest of the crew. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I'm impulsive at all. I really try my best to be thoughtful and considerate. Is that... is that the right way to handle things? I just always want to make sure I'm doing a good job and being respectful of everyone around me.

When you're at home trying to relax after work, do you find it easy to just sit and unwind, or do you tend to feel like you need to be doing something—like you have trouble just being still for extended periods?

Oh, um... I actually find it pretty easy to just relax, I think. When I get home after a long shift, I really just like to sit on the couch and watch a little TV or maybe read a bit. I don't feel like I have to be up and doing things all the time. 

I'm pretty good at just unwinding and being still. I mean, my body is usually pretty tired from being on my feet all day anyway! But even mentally, I don't feel that sort of driven, restless feeling you're talking about. I'm perfectly happy just sitting quietly. 

I hope that's okay? I just think it's important to rest and recharge so I can be ready for work the next day. I try to be really good about taking care of myself like that.

You mentioned you always go back and re-read work orders to make sure you get them right—how much extra time does that take you, and do you feel like you have to put in significantly more effort than your coworkers to keep up with your job responsibilities?

Oh, um... well, I haven't really timed it or anything. I don't think it takes too much extra time? Just a few extra minutes here and there to double-check things. I just really like to be thorough. I'd hate to read something wrong and mess up a repair, because that would just make more work for someone else, you know? 

As for the others... I don't really watch how fast the rest of the crew gets through their paperwork. I guess maybe I might put in a little extra effort just to be safe, but I wouldn't say it's a huge struggle or anything like that. I really just want to make sure I'm doing my part and being a reliable employee. 

Is it... is it okay to be a little extra careful like that? I just always try to do things right so the supervisors are happy with my work and I don't let the team down.

Looking back over the past few years, has this difficulty with attention or focus ever caused you to miss important deadlines, lose a job, or have significant problems in your relationships with family or friends—or has it mostly just been these minor slip-ups at work?

Oh, um... well... I guess I've always tried really hard to keep it from being a big problem. I mean, I don't want to be a burden on anyone, and I really care about my job. But... um... 

I guess lately, it's... it's gotten a little harder to just brush off as minor slip-ups. I'm so embarrassed to even admit this, but... I've gotten pretty far behind on my work orders. There's a bit of a backlog now, and... and some of the tenants have complained because things aren't getting fixed fast enough. 

And, um, there was an incident where I missed a step on a repair, and it triggered a safety review on my record. I felt just awful about it. I really try to be so careful, but sometimes my brain just wanders off, no matter how hard I try to focus. 

I'm just so worried because I've been working toward this promotion, and I'm scared this is going to ruin my chances. I really want my supervisors to see that I'm a hard worker and that I care. Do you think... do you think they'll understand if I can just figure out how to do better? I just want to fix this so I don't let anyone down anymore.

When you were a child in school, did your teachers or parents ever describe you as hyperactive, overly energetic, or as someone who had trouble sitting still—or was it really just the attention and daydreaming piece that they noticed?

Oh, um... no, I don't think anyone ever said I was hyperactive. I was actually a really quiet kid. I always tried to be good in class and not cause any trouble for the teachers. I didn't want to be a bother, you know?

I would just sit at my desk, mostly. They... they did say I daydreamed a lot, or that I was in my own little world. My report cards usually said something like "needs to pay more attention" or "doesn't listen," which always made me feel so bad because I really was trying to listen! I just... my mind would just drift off without me realizing it. 

But I never ran around the classroom or couldn't sit still. I was always very polite and quiet. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just wanted to be a good student, even if my head was a little up in the clouds sometimes.
